question: What is the primary function of a Health Information System in a clinical setting?

options.A: Replacing all direct bedside nursing assessments with automated scans
options.B: Eliminating the need for interprofessional verbal communication
options.C: Integrating data collection, processing, and reporting for effective care
options.D: Managing financial budgets and hospital employee payroll structures

explanation: A Health Information System is designed to manage clinical and administrative data to support overall healthcare delivery and service effectiveness. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why has digital literacy become essential for modern clinical nurses?

options.A: It ensures faster access to vital signs, laboratory trends, and physician orders
options.B: It removes the requirement for ongoing physical patient assessments
options.C: It completely prevents any human documentation errors from occurring
options.D: It allows nurses to diagnose complex medical conditions without a doctor

explanation: Digital tools streamline documentation and allow immediate retrieval of critical patient data, which directly supports safe clinical decision-making. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: What distinguishes an Electronic Health Record from a traditional paper chart?

options.A: It provides a longitudinal view of health history aggregated from multiple disciplines
options.B: It requires physical storage rooms within every hospital department
options.C: It can only be edited by attending physicians and pharmacists
options.D: It is restricted solely to outpatient surgical clinic documentation

explanation: EHRs consolidate comprehensive health data over time across various healthcare providers and departments into one digital platform. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: A nurse checking a patient's documented drug allergies within an EHR is interacting with which core component?
explanation: Active prescriptions, historical administrations, and allergy alerts are housed within the medication profile section of an EHR. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Clinical Decision Support System?

options.A: Scheduling nursing shift rosters and managing annual leave requests
options.B: Tracking hospital supply inventory and ordering surgical consumables
options.C: Automating the complete discharge billing process without human review
options.D: Generating targeted clinical advice, reminders, or alerts based on patient data

explanation: CDSS tools analyze real-time patient data to provide actionable alerts and evidence-based guidance to clinicians. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which scenario best illustrates the practical application of a CDSS in nursing care?

options.A: A database storing the academic credentials and licensure renewals of staff
options.B: A system warning a nurse about a potential drug-allergy interaction before administration
options.C: A software program automatically printing the daily hospital meal menu for patients
options.D: An application tracking the physical distance a nurse walks during a 12-hour shift

explanation: Safety alerts regarding drug interactions or allergies are classic examples of CDSS functionality protecting patients from harm. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary function of Bar Code Medication Administration technology?

options.A: Ordering new medication supplies directly from the hospital pharmacy
options.B: Calculating the exact financial cost of pharmaceuticals used during a shift
options.C: Printing physical paper labels for intravenous fluid bags
options.D: Verifying patient identity and medication details prior to administration

explanation: BCMA cross-references the patient wristband with the medication barcode to ensure the correct drug is given to the correct person. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing an intravenous infusion using a device with a built-in dose error reduction system. What type of technology is being used?
explanation: Smart pumps contain software libraries and dose limitation protocols designed to prevent programming errors during intravenous therapy. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: How does telehealth primarily improve healthcare delivery in remote regions?

options.A: By manufacturing low-cost pharmaceutical drugs locally within rural clinics
options.B: By utilizing telecommunications to deliver clinical services across distances
options.C: By eliminating the need for any physical diagnostic equipment
options.D: By replacing all community health workers with automated kiosks

explanation: Telehealth overcomes geographical barriers by connecting patients and providers through digital communication channels. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary role of a nurse managing a Remote Patient Monitoring program?

options.A: Repairing faulty digital sensors and calibrating home medical hardware
options.B: Managing the financial billing cycles for telecommunication service providers
options.C: Reviewing transmitted physiological metrics to intervene before acute deterioration occurs
options.D: Visiting every enrolled patient's household daily to perform manual physical assessments

explanation: RPM allows nurses to track chronic disease data remotely and catch early warning signs of complications. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the purpose of role-based access controls within a health information system?

options.A: Restricting user access to only the specific data necessary for their job duties
options.B: Assigning physical parking spaces to hospital staff members
options.C: Determining the monthly salary scale for different healthcare professionals
options.D: Establishing the hierarchical management structure of the nursing unit

explanation: Role-based access ensures that staff members can only view records relevant to their specific clinical or administrative responsibilities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which practice represents a direct breach of patient data security in a digital hospital environment?

options.A: Reviewing laboratory results assigned to your own directly assigned patients
options.B: Leaving an active patient workstation logged in and unattended while stepping away
options.C: Using encrypted institutional messaging applications to consult a physician
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record system after completing documentation

explanation: Unattended workstations expose confidential health records to unauthorized individuals walking by, violating patient privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is a common infrastructural challenge faced when adopting health technology in developing regions?

options.A: An absolute excess of surplus computer hardware
options.B: Unreliable power supply and internet connectivity
options.C: Instantaneous and universal staff acceptance of software
options.D: The complete absence of any digital data storage needs

explanation: Infrastructural deficits such as power outages and poor network access remain major obstacles to digital health adoption. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which strategy is most effective for overcoming staff resistance during the implementation of a new electronic health record system?

options.A: Providing comprehensive training programs and involving frontline nurses in system customization
options.B: Punishing staff members who express hesitation about using digital charting
options.C: Mandating software use immediately without offering prior technical orientation
options.D: Completely abandoning paper backups overnight without any contingency plan

explanation: Engaging end-users and providing robust education builds confidence and reduces anxiety surrounding new clinical technologies. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)
